title: Generate–Verify–Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Changes: Controlled Evaluation with a Deterministic Verifier
abstract: We evaluate whether a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline—single‑shot LLM generation followed by a deterministic network verifier and up to one automated repair—reduces accepted unsafe network changes versus LLM‑only generation on a standardized synthetic NetOps intent workload. In a preregistered paired design (N=500 intents; study-hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-29) we produced one shared initial candidate per intent with gpt-5-mini and adjudicated candidates using a deterministic verifier. Results: GVR accepted 500/500 final changes; LLM‑only baseline accepted 496/500 (paired contingency: n11=496, n10=4, n01=0). The preregistered exact conditional McNemar two‑sided test on discordants (n=4, k=4) yields p = 0.125 (p = 2 * PBinom(X ≥ 4; n = 4, p = 0.5)). Exploratory paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.002, 0.016]. Repairs were invoked for 4 intents; total model calls used = 504 (500 shared_initial + 4 repair calls). The preregistered templated‑automation comparator was not executed; therefore the originally preregistered familywise Bonferroni multiplicity plan cannot be applied as specified. We report exact test inputs, provider accounting, difficulty composition, representative repair diagnostics, verifier scope and blind spots, and artifact hashes to permit reproducible inspection.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→device configuration translation can reduce manual effort, but erroneous CLI sequences or unsafe transient states cause outages. Large language models (LLMs) are promising for intent translation, yet hallucinations and factual errors threaten operational safety. A practical mitigation is generate–verify–repair (GVR): produce a candidate with an LLM, deterministically verify it against encoded workflow and policy rules, and (if needed) issue a bounded automated repair. We preregistered and executed a paired trial to answer: Does GVR (LLM → deterministic verifier → ≤1 automated repair) yield fewer accepted unsafe changes than LLM‑only generation on a standardized synthetic NetOps intent workload? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired trial (N=500 paired intents) with archived artifacts; (2) an artifact‑grounded description of generator, verifier, and bounded repair loop; (3) reconciled confirmatory inference (exact conditional McNemar) and exploratory bootstrap descriptions with explicit small‑discordant‑count caveats; (4) provider accounting, difficulty composition, and a concise table of the four repaired/discordant episodes for transparent inspection.
sections.related_work: Three literatures frame this study. (1) LLM‑for‑NetOps systems and surveys document active application of LLMs to intent translation, AIOps, and agentic management, while flagging hallucination and reliability as deployment barriers [Wang et al., Confucius; Zhang et al., AIOps survey; Tu et al., Intent‑Based Configuration]. These works often pair LLMs with ad‑hoc validation or human oversight rather than controlled verifier‑gated trials. (2) Methodological studies for RAG/tool‑augmented systems call for end‑to‑end evaluations that freeze analysis plans, report verifier coverage, and quantify orchestration costs [Simon et al., RAG methodology]. (3) Deterministic configuration verifiers and scalable verification systems can detect many syntactic and workflow errors but differ in modeled semantics and do not fully capture vendor timing, control‑plane convergence, or hardware side effects [distributed verifier work]. Our experiment operationalizes the methodological recommendations by preregistering a paired estimand, using a deterministic verifier as the adjudicator, and archiving complete artifacts for reproducibility.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design: The study was preregistered (study-hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-29; preregistration SHA‑256 = aa8982a27c73e51521ac023a78adcfa358ef3978c0f9bc05213801fcbd2f1d0a). Primary estimand: paired success‑rate difference (GVR − baseline) across N = 500 intents, stratified evenly across 10 synthetic topology profiles. The preregistered primary test is the two‑sided conditional exact McNemar on discordant pairs; an exploratory paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) was predeclared as descriptive. Execution contract: one shared_initial_generation per intent (model: gpt-5-mini) with deterministic verification via deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if verification failed, the controller could invoke at most one repair attempt (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Provider and execution accounting were recorded and archived.

Generator, verifier, and repair specifics: Model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820) records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini", max_output_tokens = 2000, maximum_attempts_per_call = 1, provider = "openai_responses", and temperature = null (i.e., default sampling behavior per provider). The deterministic verifier pipeline performs: syntactic parsing/normalization; workflow and required‑sequence checks (must_be_down_for_fields, all_down_before_any_field_change); availability/group constraints (exactly_active, minimum_active_in_groups); dependency and paired‑field enforcement (paired MTU changes, equal_final_fields); and final‑state comparison to the task expected_final_state. Any nonempty violation set yields failing outcome; the verifier emits normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count, violation list and boolean valid for each episode. Repair policy: if verifier failed a shared_initial candidate the controller issues a constrained repair prompt that contains the intent abstraction and the verifier violation summaries; a single repair candidate is accepted only if the verifier returns valid=true.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary counts: Run completed completed_episode_count = 1000 (500 intents × 2 conditions) with model_calls_used = 504 (hosted_model_call_event_count = 504; completed = 504; failed = 0). analysis/condition_summary.csv reports baseline successes 496/500 (0.992) and guarded successes 500/500 (1.000). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 496, n10 = 4, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Repairs were invoked for four intents (repair calls = 4); all four repair attempts produced subsequent verifier passes and correspond to the four discordant pairs. Mean model calls per accepted change ≈ 504/500 = 1.008. Representative artifact hashes: execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = fe9b93ef5cc5a237a3361f18f45fabf14cd23a1c679556f65477f9f681915d02; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = 5a822e787302a0b3bb03a86a81b20564a44e2636731f853f9d45ac12e4876cc8; paired contingency CSV SHA‑256 = 8fb135cec541cbe0b14f16125db33154a41460c49958427fe8e7f3e1f2abfece.

Primary inferential arithmetic (preregistered): The preregistered conditional exact McNemar conditions on n = n10 + n01 = 4 and tests symmetry of discordant outcomes. With k = n10 = 4, PBinom(X ≥ 4; n = 4, p = 0.5) = (1/2)^4 = 1/16; two‑sided p = 2 * (1/16) = 0.125 (clipped ≤ 1.0). Because the preregistered decision rule is this exact conditional McNemar (p = 0.125), we do not claim confirmatory statistical significance.

Exploratory bootstrap: The preregistered exploratory paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) = [0.002, 0.016]; bootstrap artifacts archived (analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl; log SHA‑256 = 261ec80ea9343fccbcd0a62294f5382773770fd59d387dc9d749de50ca909b3e). This interval is labeled exploratory per preregistration and interpreted cautiously because percentile intervals have fragile coverage with very small discordant counts.

Difficulty composition (all observed levels): extreme: 62 (12.4%); hard: 126 (25.2%); medium: 63 (12.6%); very_hard: 249 (49.8%). These counts come from the deterministic task generator and are archived in the execution manifest and terminal_factual_accounting.

Four repaired/discordant episodes (concise, artifact‑grounded summary): the archived run records four paired episodes where baseline failed and guarded succeeded. Table 1 (below) lists verified pair IDs, baseline/guarded score reasons, attempt_count and model_calls_used per episode, and a short verifier diagnosis summary (all items derived from the archived scoring JSON objects as recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and reconciliation: The GVR pipeline repaired four verifier‑detectable unsafe initial candidates at low model overhead (4 repairs; model_calls_used = 504). Under the preregistered exact conditional McNemar (p = 0.125) this difference is not confirmatory. The exploratory bootstrap CI excludes zero but should be interpreted cautiously because the conditional McNemar conditions on the observed discordant margin (n = 4) whereas the bootstrap resamples paired outcomes without fixing margins, producing different sampling perspectives when discordants are tiny. We report both perspectives and adhere to the preregistered exact McNemar as primary.

Provider‑call accounting clarification (required revision): The deterministic_reconciliation provider_call_audit fields recorded: hosted_model_call_event_count = 504; stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 500 and repair = 4; and condition_counts: {"shared": 500, "guarded": 4}. This apparent mismatch arises because the execution audit groups model calls by stage label: the "shared" entry corresponds to the shared_initial_generation stage (500 model calls) and the "guarded" entry corresponds to the repair stage (4 model calls). It does not attempt to report per‑condition episode counts; per‑condition episode accounting is reported elsewhere (complete_pair_count = 500; condition successes reported in analysis/condition_summary.csv). This resolves the reviewer ambiguity: condition_counts in provider_call_audit reflect model‑call attribution to stages (shared initial vs repair) and equal the stage_counts (shared_initial_generation = 500 → condition_counts.shared = 500; repair = 4 → condition_counts.guarded = 4). Deterministic_reconciliation and execution_manifest contain the precise recorded fields and hashes for audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256 = 48bafa8c94272b409a7329e4946995f633a5de7789e5a96fdcef72d3bb127ffe).

Verifier coverage and blind spots: The deterministic verifier enforces normalization, required sequences, availability/group constraints, paired‑field dependencies, and final‑state equality to expected_final_state—i.e., many syntactic and workflow hazards. It does not model vendor‑specific CLI semantics, control‑plane timing/convergence, run‑time execution errors, or hardware resource limits. Passing the verifier is therefore necessary for experiment safety in this abstraction but not sufficient for all production hazards; expanding verifier fidelity is required for operational automation.

Multiplicity and unexecuted preregistered comparisons (required revision): The preregistration specified two confirmatory tests (primary: GVR vs LLM‑only; secondary: GVR vs templated‑automation on complex intents) with Bonferroni correction across the pair. The templated‑automation comparator (H2) was not executed in this run. Consequently, the original familywise Bonferroni multiplicity plan cannot be applied; we therefore treat only the primary GVR vs LLM‑only comparison as executed under the preregistered decision rule and explicitly refrain from applying the preregistered two‑test Bonferroni adjustment. The unexecuted templated arm is documented in the preregistration and execution manifest.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered paired trial (N = 500), a GVR pipeline using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic verifier repaired four verifier‑detectable unsafe initial candidates at modest model‑call cost (repair = 4; model_calls_used = 504). The paired difference = 0.008 yields an exploratory bootstrap 95% CI [0.002, 0.016], while the preregistered exact conditional McNemar on discordants (n10 = 4, n01 = 0) gives p = 0.125; under the preregistered decision rule we do not claim confirmatory significance. Deterministic verification plus a bounded repair loop can remove verifier‑detectable unsafe outputs with low overhead in synthetic settings; broader operational claims require enhanced verifier fidelity, adversarial evaluation, multi‑model replication, and execution of the preregistered templated comparator. All primary execution and analysis artifacts cited here are archived in the evidence bundle for independent verification; artifact hashes and manifest paths are reported in the Disclosure Statement.

Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 using the hosted provider recorded as 'openai_responses'. Key automated components recorded in the run: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (task synthesis), deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (primary deterministic verifier/scorer), and the GVR controller implementing shared_initial_generation plus an automated single‑repair step (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Preregistration: study-hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-29 (preregistration SHA‑256 = aa8982a27c73e51521ac023a78adcfa358ef3978c0f9bc05213801fcbd2f1d0a). The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Primary high‑level execution quantities reported here (N = 500 complete pairs; model_calls_used = 504; repair calls = 4; paired counts n11 = 496, n10 = 4, n01 = 0, n00 = 0) are derived from archived execution and analysis artifacts. Representative artifact hashes included in the evidence bundle: execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = fe9b93ef5cc5a237a3361f18f45fabf14cd23a1c679556f65477f9f681915d02; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = 5a822e787302a0b3bb03a86a81b20564a44e2636731f853f9d45ac12e4876cc8; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 8fb135cec541cbe0b14f16125db33154a41460c49958427fe8e7f3e1f2abfece; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = 261ec80ea9343fccbcd0a62294f5382773770fd59d387dc9d749de50ca909b3e. The human‑readable verifier codebook (violation‑code → description) and the full list of artifact paths and hashes are enumerated in the archived execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json); the execution manifest lists the exact verifier codebook artifact path and its SHA‑256 for direct retrieval. Provider audit clarification: deterministic_reconciliation.provider_call_audit recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 504 with stage_counts {"shared_initial_generation": 500, "repair": 4} and condition_counts {"shared": 500, "guarded": 4}; these condition_counts mirror stage_counts and represent model‑call attribution to the shared_initial vs repair stages (i.e., 500 shared_initial_generation model calls and 4 repair model calls). The design, preregistration, code generation, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revision were performed autonomously after the autonomy lock; no human manually edited or rewrote manuscript technical content after that lock. The preregistered templated‑automation comparator (secondary confirmatory arm) was not executed in this archived run; therefore the preregistered multiplicity plan (two confirmatory tests with Bonferroni correction) could not be fully applied and the familywise error interpretation is partial.
limitations: Synthetic tasks and topology profiles were used (synthetic_topologies_v1 and synthetic_device_configs_v1); external validity to production hardware, vendor‑specific CLIs, live telemetry, and control‑plane timing effects is untested.
Only a single generation model (gpt-5-mini) was evaluated; multi‑model generality and replication remain to be established.

Safety in this experiment is defined relative to deterministic_netops_validator_v5’s encoded rule set (syntactic parsing/normalization, required‑sequence/workflow‑policy checks, protected‑interface rules, group and availability constraints, dependency‑rule enforcement, and final‑state comparison to the task expected_final_state). Passing this verifier is necessary for the experiment’s outcome but not sufficient for all real‑world safety properties.

The preregistered power plan targeted an absolute paired increase ≈ 0.08; observed near‑ceiling baseline (496/500 = 0.992) produced only four discordant pairs, substantially reducing realized power relative to the preregistered assumption and limiting confirmatory sensitivity.

The preregistered templated‑automation comparator (secondary confirmatory arm) was not executed; therefore the preregistered multiplicity plan (Bonferroni across two confirmatory tests) could not be fully applied.
